title: विश्व के कई हिस्सों में भीषण गर्मी की लहरों से भारी नुकसान होता है। - Vietnam.vn

full_text:
विश्व के कई हिस्सों में भीषण गर्मी की लहरों से भारी नुकसान होता है।
दक्षिण कोरिया में भीषण गर्मी से कम से कम 31 लोगों की मौत हो गई है, 9 लाख से अधिक पशुधन और 14 लाख पाली गई मछलियाँ मर गई हैं; अत्यधिक उच्च तापमान के कारण आलू, तरबूज और पौधों की फसलें खराब हो जाने से कई किसानों की फसलें बर्बाद हो गई हैं।
VietnamPlus•14/08/2026
यूरोप और एशिया के कई क्षेत्रों में भीषण गर्मी की लहरों के कारण गंभीर नुकसान हो रहा है, जिसमें आर्थिक नुकसान में वृद्धि, बिजली आपूर्ति प्रभावित होना, फसलों का विनाश और जंगल में आग लगना शामिल है।
फ्रांस में पर्यावरण मंत्री मोनिका बारबट ने 12 अगस्त को कहा कि इस गर्मी की लू से प्रत्यक्ष और अप्रत्यक्ष नुकसान 10-15 अरब यूरो (11.5-17.2 अरब अमेरिकी डॉलर) तक पहुंच सकता है। यह केवल एक प्रारंभिक अनुमान है और लू जारी रहने के कारण इसमें और वृद्धि हो सकती है। बारबट के अनुसार, यह नुकसान 2022 में हुए लगभग 5-6 अरब यूरो के नुकसान से कहीं अधिक होगा, जब इस वर्ष की लू अधिक लंबी और गंभीर थी।
क्रोएशिया में, स्प्लिट शहर में 12 अगस्त को तापमान 39.7 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया, जो अब तक का सबसे अधिक तापमान है और जून में दर्ज किए गए पिछले रिकॉर्ड 39.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस को पार कर गया है। लंबे समय से चल रही भीषण गर्मी और सूखे के कारण डेन्यूब और द्रावा नदियों में जलस्तर कम हो गया है, जिससे जलमार्ग परिवहन प्रभावित हुआ है। साल की शुरुआत से 10 अगस्त तक, क्रोएशिया में 8,832 जंगल में आग लगने की घटनाएं दर्ज की गईं, जो पिछले साल की इसी अवधि की तुलना में लगभग 13% अधिक है।
रोमानिया में, डेन्यूब नदी का जलस्तर रिकॉर्ड निचले स्तर पर पहुँच गया, जिसके चलते देश को 13 अगस्त को चेर्नावोडा परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र की इकाई 2 को नियंत्रित रूप से बंद करना पड़ा। इकाई 1 जुलाई के अंत से ही बंद थी। यह संयंत्र सामान्यतः रोमानिया के कुल बिजली उत्पादन का लगभग पाँचवाँ हिस्सा आपूर्ति करता है।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
हंगरी में, अधिकारी पाक्स परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र के आसपास जल स्तर बनाए रखने के लिए भी उपाय लागू कर रहे हैं।
दक्षिण कोरिया में, अगस्त की शुरुआत में यांगसान शहर में तापमान 42.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक पहुंच गया, जो 1904 में आधुनिक तापमान रिकॉर्ड शुरू होने के बाद से सबसे अधिक है। इस भीषण गर्मी के कारण कम से कम 31 लोगों की मौत हो गई और 9 लाख से अधिक पशुधन और 14 लाख पाली गई मछलियां मर गईं। अत्यधिक तापमान के कारण आलू, तरबूज और पौधों को नुकसान पहुंचने से कई किसानों की फसलें बर्बाद हो गईं।
जापान में कई क्षेत्रों में 40 डिग्री सेल्सियस या उससे अधिक तापमान दर्ज किया गया, जबकि देश ने पहली बार 40 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक तापमान वाले दिनों को संदर्भित करने के लिए कोकुशोबी (अत्यधिक गर्म दिन) शब्द का इस्तेमाल किया।
हांगकांग (चीन) में भी 36.9 डिग्री सेल्सियस तापमान दर्ज किया गया, जो 1884 में आंकड़े दर्ज किए जाने के बाद से अब तक का सबसे अधिक तापमान है। वैज्ञानिकों का मानना है कि जलवायु परिवर्तन इस क्षेत्र में भीषण गर्मी की लहरों की तीव्रता को बढ़ा रहा है।
इस बीच, कनाडा में ब्रिटिश कोलंबिया में जंगल की आग लगातार फैल रही है, जिसके चलते लगभग 20,000 लोगों को सुरक्षित स्थानों पर पहुंचाया गया है और एक व्यक्ति की जान चली गई है। प्रांत भर में 100 से अधिक जगहों पर आग लगी हुई है, जिनमें बाल्ड रेंज की आग दमकलकर्मियों के लिए एक बड़ी चुनौती पेश कर रही है। आग बुझाने में मेक्सिको के 100 कर्मियों सहित लगभग 193 दमकलकर्मी लगे हुए हैं।

title: 14 अगस्त के लिए मौसम का पूर्वानुमान: दिन में भीषण गर्मी, शाम को तेज आंधी-तूफान। - Vietnam.vn

full_text:
राष्ट्रीय मौसम विज्ञान एवं जल विज्ञान पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के अनुसार, 14 अगस्त को उत्तरी और मध्य वियतनाम के एक बड़े क्षेत्र में भीषण गर्मी का प्रकोप जारी रहेगा। विशेष रूप से, थान्ह होआ से लेकर दक्षिण मध्य तट तक के कई क्षेत्रों में भीषण गर्मी पड़ सकती है। वहीं दूसरी ओर, दोपहर और शाम के समय कई क्षेत्रों में गरज के साथ बारिश होने की संभावना है, और कुछ स्थानों पर भारी वर्षा भी हो सकती है।
हनोई में गर्म और धूप वाला मौसम बना रहेगा, दोपहर में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ने की संभावना है, और कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश हो सकती है। रात में भी कुछ स्थानों पर बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी।
उत्तरी वियतनाम में दिन भर गर्म मौसम बना रहेगा, कुछ इलाकों में तापमान 36 डिग्री सेल्सियस से अधिक रहेगा। दोपहर और शाम को उत्तर-पश्चिम और उत्तर-पूर्व दोनों क्षेत्रों में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ बौछारें पड़ेंगी; उत्तर-पूर्व क्षेत्र में अधिक वर्षा होने की संभावना है, कुछ इलाकों में भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है।
मध्य वियतनाम में भीषण गर्मी का प्रकोप जारी है। थान्ह होआ से लेकर ह्यू तक के इलाकों में भीषण गर्मी पड़ रही है, वहीं दक्षिण मध्य तट पर भी तापमान अधिक बना हुआ है। गरज के साथ बारिश मुख्य रूप से दोपहर और शाम के समय होती है; थान्ह होआ और न्घे आन प्रांतों में दोपहर के बाद से छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ बारिश होने की संभावना है।
दक्षिण, मध्य हाइलैंड्स, दक्षिणी वियतनाम और हो ची मिन्ह सिटी में दिन के दौरान धूप खिली रहेगी, लेकिन शाम को बारिश शुरू हो जाएगी। छिटपुट बौछारें और गरज के साथ बारिश होगी, कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है।
गौरतलब है कि आंधी-तूफान तेजी से विकसित हो सकते हैं और इनके साथ बवंडर, बिजली, ओले और तेज हवा के झोंके भी आ सकते हैं। आंधी-तूफान के दौरान लोगों को बाहरी गतिविधियों को सीमित करना चाहिए और अपनी सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करने के लिए एहतियाती उपाय करने चाहिए।
14 अगस्त को विभिन्न क्षेत्रों के लिए मौसम का पूर्वानुमान:
हनोई शहर
न्यूनतम तापमान: 27-29 डिग्री। अधिकतम तापमान: 34-36 डिग्री।
आसमान में बादल छाए रहेंगे और रात में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है; दिन में गर्मी और धूप रहेगी, दोपहर में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है, और कुछ क्षेत्रों में भारी बारिश हो सकती है। हवा हल्की रहेगी। गरज के साथ तूफान के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली, ओले और तेज हवा के झोंके चलने की संभावना है।
उत्तर-पश्चिमी वियतनाम
न्यूनतम तापमान: 25-28 डिग्री सेल्सियस, कुछ स्थानों पर 24 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे। अधिकतम तापमान: 33-36 डिग्री सेल्सियस, कुछ स्थानों पर 36 डिग्री सेल्सियस से ऊपर; विशेष रूप से लाई चाऊ और डिएन बिएन में: 30-32 डिग्री सेल्सियस, कुछ स्थानों पर 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस से ऊपर।
आपको यह भी पसंद आ सकता है
आसमान में बादल छाए रहेंगे और रात में कुछ इलाकों में, खासकर उत्तर-पश्चिमी क्षेत्र में, छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है; दिन में गर्मी और धूप रहेगी (डिएन बिएन और लाई चाऊ को छोड़कर), कल दोपहर में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है, और कुछ स्थानों पर भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है। हवा हल्की रहेगी। गरज के साथ तूफान के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली, ओले और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है।
पूर्वोत्तर वियतनाम
न्यूनतम तापमान: 26-29 डिग्री सेल्सियस, कुछ पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में 25 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे। अधिकतम तापमान: 33-36 डिग्री सेल्सियस, कुछ क्षेत्रों में 36 डिग्री सेल्सियस से ऊपर, पूर्वोत्तर क्षेत्र को छोड़कर जहां यह 31-34 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहेगा।
कल रात कुछ इलाकों में बादल छाए रहेंगे और छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है। दिन में गर्मी और धूप रहेगी, दोपहर में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है, और कुछ स्थानों पर भारी बारिश हो सकती है। पूर्वोत्तर क्षेत्र में छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है, साथ ही कुछ स्थानों पर भारी बारिश भी हो सकती है (बारिश दोपहर और रात में केंद्रित रहेगी)। हवा हल्की रहेगी। गरज के साथ तूफान के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली, ओले और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है।
थान्ह होआ से ह्यू
न्यूनतम तापमान: 26-29 डिग्री। अधिकतम तापमान: 34-37 डिग्री, कुछ क्षेत्रों में 37 डिग्री से अधिक भी हो सकता है।
आसमान में बादल छाए रहेंगे और शाम व रात में कुछ इलाकों में, विशेषकर थान्ह होआ और न्घे आन प्रांतों में, छिटपुट बारिश और गरज के साथ तूफान आने की संभावना है; दिन में धूप खिली रहेगी और गर्मी रहेगी, कुछ इलाकों में भीषण गर्मी पड़ सकती है। दक्षिण-पश्चिम दिशा से 2-3 तीव्रता की हवाएं चलेंगी। गरज के साथ तूफान के दौरान बवंडर, बिजली गिरने, ओले पड़ने और तेज हवा के झोंके आने की संभावना है।

full_text:
रिकॉर्ड तोड़ तापमान और भीषण सूखे के कारण यूरोप और विश्व का कृषि क्षेत्र एक नए संकट में फंस गया है।
भीषण गर्मी और सूखा वैश्विक कृषि उत्पादकता के लिए खतरा पैदा करते हैं।
जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण सूखा पड़ रहा है, जिससे कृषि उत्पादन पर काफी असर पड़ रहा है, खाद्य पदार्थों की कीमतें बढ़ रही हैं और यूरोप तथा दुनिया भर में आपूर्ति श्रृंखलाएं बाधित हो रही हैं।
संयुक्त राष्ट्र खाद्य एवं कृषि संगठन (एफएओ) और यूरोपीय संघ के संयुक्त अनुसंधान केंद्र (जेआरसी) की चेतावनियों के अनुसार, जलवायु परिवर्तन सीधे तौर पर ग्रीष्म और शीत ऋतु दोनों की फसलों की पैदावार को खतरे में डाल रहा है, जिससे आपूर्ति में कमी और खाद्य पदार्थों की कीमतों में वृद्धि का खतरा पैदा हो रहा है।
एफएओ के अद्यतन आंकड़ों से पता चलता है कि वैश्विक अनाज मूल्य सूचकांक में मात्र एक महीने में 3.4% की वृद्धि हुई है। विशेष रूप से गेहूं की कीमतों में 5.8% की वृद्धि हुई है, जिसका कारण काला सागर के रास्ते निर्यात में व्यवधान और प्रमुख उत्पादक देशों पर चरम मौसम के प्रभाव को लेकर चिंताएं हैं।
अमेरिका में शुष्क और गर्म मौसम के कारण मक्के की कीमतों में भी 3.6% की वृद्धि हुई, जबकि यूरोपीय संघ में लंबे समय तक गर्म मौसम और एशिया में अल नीनो के प्रभावों के कारण चीनी की कीमतों में 5.6% की वृद्धि हुई।
इसके अलावा, घटते जलस्तर के कारण डेन्यूब और राइन जैसी महत्वपूर्ण जलधाराएं माल परिवहन के लिए दुर्गम हो गई हैं, जिससे आपूर्ति श्रृंखला में व्यवधान का खतरा और बढ़ गया है।
यूरोप में, जेआरसी की रिपोर्ट से पता चलता है कि मई से जुलाई तक लगातार चलने वाली भीषण गर्मी की लहरों ने मिट्टी की नमी को कम कर दिया है और पानी की गंभीर कमी का दबाव बढ़ा दिया है। यह स्थिति पश्चिमी, मध्य और पूर्वी यूरोप में ग्रीष्म और शीतकालीन दोनों फसलों की पैदावार की संभावनाओं को बुरी तरह प्रभावित कर रही है।
गौरतलब है कि मध्य और उत्तरी इटली के प्रमुख कृषि क्षेत्र भी गर्मी के तनाव और पानी की कमी से सबसे बुरी तरह प्रभावित क्षेत्रों में शामिल हैं।
उत्पादकता में यह गिरावट न केवल "मेड इन इटली" कृषि उत्पादों के लिए सीधा खतरा है, बल्कि पहले से ही अस्थिर भू-राजनीतिक और ऊर्जा परिदृश्य के बीच वैश्विक स्तर पर उपभोक्ताओं के लिए जीवन यापन की लागत को भी बढ़ाती है।

शामली। जिले में अधिकतम तापमान में चार डिग्री सेल्सियस की कमी आई है, लेकिन लोगों को गर्मी और उमस से राहत नहीं मिल पाई। पिछले 24 घंटे में अधिकतम तापमान 31 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया, जबकि न्यूनतम तापमान 28 डिग्री सेल्सियस पर स्थिर बना रहा।

Temperatures are forecast to hit 34C (93F) in parts of south-east England on Friday as the UK's fifth widespread heatwave of the year continues - but it is predicted to be the last day of sweltering temperatures for most people.
Amber heat-health alerts issued by the UK Health Security Agency remain in force across all of England until 21:00 BST, warning of ongoing significant impacts across health and social care services.
However, temperatures in northern and western areas of the country will be noticeably lower than Thursday, which was the hottest day of 2026.
And that wil be followed by much cooler conditions for all parts over the weekend as this heatwave is brought to a quick end.
Hottest in the east on Friday
Kew Gardens in London reached 38.1C on Thursday, making it the UK's hottest day of 2026 so far, and the fifth hottest UK day on record.
It is also the second time this year that the temperature has reached 38C, after Lingwood, Norfolk recorded 38.0C on 26 June.
This is only the second time that 38C has been reached twice in the same year - the previous occasion being 2022.
Though the Met Office amber warning for extreme heat that covered large swathes of England on Thursday expired at midnight, high temperatures will linger in central and eastern parts of England on Friday.
Long spells of sunshine will lift temperatures to 29-34C (84-93F) across large parts of the Midlands, Lincolnshire, East Anglia and the south-east.
For many places it will mark a third consecutive day above official heatwave thresholds.
The heat will ease elsewhere.
Somewhat cooler conditions will begin to move into northern and western parts of the UK, although temperatures will generally remain above the norm for the time of year - widely reaching the low to mid-20s Celsius.
Many places will be dry with a mix of cloud and sunny spells although a few showers are possible, and these could be heavy and thundery in some places.
When will the heatwave end?
While Saturday will still feel very warm in south-eastern areas of England, temperatures will have mostly come down below the heatwave threshold of 28C, marking an end to the current heatwave.
Fresher air will then have spread to all parts of the UK with temperatures around average for the time of year by Sunday - around 17 to 26C.
It will however remain dry for most of the UK over the weekend, stretching out the run of days where there has been no notable rain in southern England for two months.
It is possible Wisley in Surrey will have notched up 60 days with no rain by Sunday.
Into next week an area of low pressure will move close to the north-west of the UK and that will bring some rain-bearing weather fronts.
Scotland and Northern Ireland will see most of the rain on Monday.
Into Tuesday, there could be some showers moving into northern England and north Wales with the possibility of those moving further south across England.
While some rain is a possibility in southern England, there is a chance that some locations in drought may continue to miss out.
You can stay up to date with the latest forecast for your area on the BBC Weather website and app.

Severe heatwave damages potato crops in Gangwon Province, South Korea
A severe heatwave alert has been issued for the Gangwon region for the first time. Damage to summer crops is severe, raising concerns that it will further drive up already high agricultural prices.
Severe damage to cabbage and potato crops
Thousands of square meters of cabbage fields have been entirely plowed under. While harvest was temporarily delayed to match market prices, the crops completely burned black.
If sold at market value, it would have been worth tens of millions of won. Even potatoes that were fine a week ago have completely rotted. No matter how much the soil is dug up, there are no healthy potatoes to be found.
In the boiling temperatures, they have turned soft and crush like boiled potatoes. In 40 years of farming, this is the first time such a thing has happened.
Lee Sang-hyuk, Haean-myeon, Yanggu-gun, Gangwon Province:
"Fields like this are not just one or two. How can words even describe it? It is just so upsetting."
A farmer examines heat-damaged potatoes in Gangwon Province, South Korea, where extreme temperatures are affecting potato and other summer crops.
Fruit crops suffer from extreme heat
Fruits could not escape the heat either. Apples are suffering from sunburns that cause scalding, and peaches are experiencing splitting damage where the fruits burst open.
Varieties that should be growing rapidly in time for the Chuseok shipment have stopped growing altogether due to the heat.
Cheon Jeong-tae, Apple Farmer:
"Chuseok is in late September, and this is not the time for them to be coloring. The sides exposed to continuous sunlight are turning red. When it gets worse, they turn white."
Severe heatwave alerts issued across Gangwon
Amid the relentless heatwave, the province's first severe heatwave alerts were issued for areas including Chuncheon, Hongcheon, and Hoengseong, but farmers cannot stop working while watching their crops burn away.
Park Won-sun, Peach Farmer:
"They tell us not to go out and work during the day, but these peaches keep rotting away, and sitting back just does not feel right."
Concerns grow over agricultural prices
Currently, damage reports are focused primarily on human casualties and livestock, making it impossible to even gauge the full extent of the damage to farming households.
As the hearts of farmers burn with the heat, an impact on agricultural prices for the upcoming Chuseok holiday appears inevitable.

Health experts issue heatwave advice to pregnant women and new mothers
Pregnant women, new mothers and families with newborn babies are being urged to take extra precautions during periods of extreme heat, as health experts warn of the risks high temperatures can pose to both mother and baby.
At the Midland Met University Hospital, 938 babies were born during June and July's heatwave period.
Pregnancy makes it harder for women to regulate their body temperature, and even a single day of extreme heat can put extra strain on mother and baby.
Research has linked heatwaves to an increased risk of premature birth and other pregnancy complications.
Newborn babies are also particularly vulnerable, as they cannot regulate their body temperature effectively and can overheat quickly.
Parents and carers are encouraged to look out for warning signs including unusual sleepiness, poor feeding, fewer wet nappies than usual, rapid breathing and feeling unusually hot.
For babies under six months old, breast milk remains the safest and most effective way to keep them hydrated during hot weather.
Katie Philpott (pictured), head of Midwifery at Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust, said: "Extreme heat is not just uncomfortable, it can pose a serious risk to pregnant women, new mothers and newborn babies. During pregnancy, the body is already working harder and coping with higher temperatures can become much more difficult, particularly during a heatwave.
“We know that hot weather can increase the risk of complications in pregnancy, including premature birth, so it is important that pregnant women take heat warnings seriously and take steps to keep cool and well hydrated.
“Newborn babies are especially vulnerable because they cannot regulate their temperature in the same way as older children and adults. Parents should keep a close eye on their baby, particularly during the hottest parts of the day, and seek advice if they are concerned about symptoms such as poor feeding, unusual sleepiness or fewer wet nappies.
"The good news is that most heat-related illness can be prevented. By staying hydrated, keeping out of the sun during the hottest hours and knowing when to seek help, families can help protect both mother and baby throughout periods of extreme heat."

The RSPCA has seen a 74% surge in pet owners calls desperate for advice about how to look after their pets during a heatwave.

"Although once in the sea that's nice and cool for them, walking across that sand is a big "no no" for dogs.
"Tarmac gets hot this time of year as well so its making sure you get up nice and early in the morning, walk the dog and then again in the evening, still being aware of that heat beneath their paws," he said.
Rich also advises putting ice cubes in the water bowl and putting food in the fridge before putting it out and making frozen treats.

The Marshall Project has been investigating the effects of extreme heat on prisons and jails for nearly a decade. As ever-rising summer temperatures make this subject more urgent, our staff compiled a toolkit to help local reporters, researchers and policymakers do the same in their communities.
Our July 2026 webinar asked a slate of national experts for their best advice on how to explore the issue — and for the facts most people don’t know about how heat impacts incarcerated people. Their tips span the climate, criminal justice, public health and immigration sectors. Here are their key findings:
Look out for underlying conditions
Not every heat-related death is heatstroke, said Susi Vassallo, M.D., a certified correctional health professional and clinical professor at NYU School of Medicine’s emergency medical department.
“Although we think of heat as causing heatstroke or heat exhaustion, there are not nearly as many of those — in the free world or in prisons — as there are worsening of underlying conditions,” Vassallo said.
According to Vassallo, medical visits, hospitalizations and deaths all increase “precipitously” in hot weather, but most of those involve people with cardiac or respiratory diseases or other chronic conditions such as diabetes. While an autopsy or death certificate may not mention heatstroke or hyperthermia as the primary cause of death, there may be heat-related conditions listed as secondary or contributing factors. Requesting death records for people who died at an un-air-conditioned facility during a heatwave and running them by a medical professional can help determine whether heat was a factor in the person’s death.
Extreme heat can be more dangerous for people with chronic conditions in prison, Vassallo said, due to their inability to control the temperature of their environment and also because there is often less access to high-quality medical care to treat symptoms when they arise. Additionally, certain demographics can be particularly vulnerable, such as older adults or people in solitary confinement.
Interrogate so-called ‘solutions’
Officials may say they have numerous mitigation measures in place to keep people from overheating in facilities without air-conditioning, but not all cooling tools are created equal. Ufuoma Ovienmhada, an assistant professor at the University of Arizona’s School of Geography, Development & Environment and founder of the Toxic Prisons Mapping Project, pointed to research indicating that “above certain temperatures, a fan makes no difference” in reducing heat exposure — and in humid climates, can actually make the heat feel worse.
Fans are also rarely provided for free, Ovienmhada said, and at some facilities can cost the equivalent of months of work on a meager prison salary. Additionally, not all cells have outlets, meaning even if someone has a fan, they can’t always use it. Other potential sources of respite, like cups of ice or cold showers, are rarely offered.
This means that “incarcerated people often resort to extreme measures of either shedding their clothes or purposefully flooding their cells with toilet water to create basically a swimming pool to cool themselves,” Ovienmhada explained, but these “heat-adaptive behaviors” are frequently met with punishment. “These same behaviors that they’re doing just to survive can result in sanctions or even being thrown into solitary confinement,” she said.
Beware the cold
Heat emergencies aren’t the only example of dangerous temperatures.
“In California, the attorney general here actually sued Los Angeles County for its jail system, and their case concerned both extreme heat and extreme cold,” said Rio Scharf, staff attorney at UC Berkeley’s Criminal Law and Justice Center. He added that there have been at least two deaths related to hypothermia in the last few years.
Extreme cold is also an issue impacting ICE detention centers, Scharf said, with ongoing litigation in several states — including California — that aims to require blankets and warmer clothing in frigid facilities. In many of those cases, he said, “either the conditions [were] naturally cold, or the AC was being blasted to make people uncomfortable.”
In her research, Ovienmhada previously told The Marshall Project that she’s heard similar instances of air-conditioning being weaponized by corrections officers to punish or coerce people.
Know the litigation
There are three major legal arguments attorneys have used to assert that extreme heat constitutes a civil rights violation, according to Scharf. First is the Eighth Amendment, which argues that the impact of extreme heat — effectively cooking people to death — constitutes cruel or unusual punishment.
Second, in the case of local jails and ICE detention centers, lawyers have also presented due process claims under the Fifth and 14th amendments, arguing that people who haven’t been found guilty of anything shouldn’t be punished at all — which includes forcing them to bake in the heat (or freeze in the cold) with no relief.
Finally, there have also been lawsuits alleging violations of the Americans with Disabilities Act, which focuses on the ways extreme heat can be “especially harmful to people with pre-existing disabilities,” Scharf said.
However, because these laws require attorneys to prove not only that harm was done, but that it was the result of deliberate indifference by the local, state or federal government, Scharf noted that even when the legal arguments are strong, “these cases are really hard to win, and you can sometimes win without actually getting any relief.”
When in doubt, ask an expert
Legal documents and other related court records can be a goldmine of information describing how exactly extreme heat affects people in carceral facilities, said Maurice Chammah, staff writer for The Marshall Project. But court filings on yearslong cases can have hundreds of entries and it can be daunting to know where to start.
“Journalists shouldn’t be afraid to reach out to counsel in the cases and ask to be directed to documents that are going to be most useful to them,” Scharf said. In his own research into the impact of extreme heat on people in California jails, Scharf said he’s requested civil grand jury reports, grievances from incarcerated people and monitoring reports from any agencies that oversee the local jails, whether a state oversight office or an independent watchdog.

Six people, including a child and three firefighters, were taken to hospital on Thursday after wildfires broke out across the West Midlands and spread into homes, on what was the hottest day recorded in the UK so far this year.
In total, ten people were injured and treated by emergency services.
The most serious blaze struck Stourbridge, Worcestershire, where a fire that began near the town’s golf club just after 1.30pm spread rapidly across around 40 acres of dry grassland before reaching houses on and around Racecourse Lane. West Midlands Fire Service said the fire appeared to have broken out in several places at once, and believes it started in the fields rather than inside any of the properties. Residents were evacuated to refuge centres at the town hall and St Michael’s Church in Norton, and police taped off homes that had been abandoned. Ambulance crews treated six members of the public at the scene; two were taken to hospital with smoke inhalation, while the other four were treated and discharged on site. The child and three firefighters were also taken to hospital.
Elsewhere in the region, homes in Oldbury were evacuated after a fire broke out near the former Brandhall Golf Course, and a woman was seriously injured as a blaze damaged properties in Castle Vale, east Birmingham. Fire crews also tackled a fire in Sandyford, Stoke-on-Trent, and in Pershore, Worcestershire, where around 30 homes were evacuated, one person was treated for smoke inhalation, and roughly 200 properties lost power before the fire was brought under control. In Warwickshire, a large wildfire in Salford Priors, near Stratford-upon-Avon, led the county’s fire and rescue service to declare a major incident, with residents told to keep doors and windows closed.
The M6 was briefly shut northbound between Castle Bromwich and Spaghetti Junction after smoke from a nearby fire drifted across the carriageway, reopening after around two hours but leaving drivers facing tailbacks of several miles and delays of up to two and a half hours. Further wildfires were reported elsewhere in the country on Thursday, including in Norfolk, South Wales and Hampshire.
Simon Tuhill, chief fire officer for West Midlands Fire Service, said the day’s incidents ranked among the most significant the service has ever had to handle, with more than 100 firefighters deployed and thousands of 999 calls received. West Midlands Ambulance Service described it as an exceptionally busy day, and asked the public to consider whether non-emergency medical issues could be dealt with through other NHS services rather than by calling 999.
Richard Parker, mayor of the West Midlands, called the situation extremely worrying and said he was concerned for evacuated families and for those whose journeys had been disrupted, while stressing that safety came first. He said the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, had pledged to support regional fire services with whatever additional resources they needed.
Mr Burnham said it was distressing to see homes and communities affected by fires across the country, and praised firefighters for working in dangerous conditions to keep others safe. He said he was in contact with local leaders and would be speaking directly to emergency services about the ongoing response.
Fire investigators are expected to examine the scenes once conditions allow, though officials said it remained too early to determine what had caused the fires.

The weather department has predicted intense rainfall in some areas of Konkan and Ghat regions today, August 14. Citizens in the districts of Konkan and Ghat areas have been advised to remain alert.
Heavy Rain Warning for Five Districts in Konkan
According to the weather department's forecast, heavy rainfall is likely in Thane, Raigad, Ratnagiri, and Sindhudurg districts. With the monsoon being active along the Konkan coast, there is a possibility of heavy showers in the coming days.
Precautions for Travelers in Ghat Areas
Heavy rainfall has also been predicted in the Ghat regions of Nashik, Pune, Satara, and Kolhapur districts. Given the risk of landslides and disruptions in transportation due to the rain, travelers have been urged to exercise caution by the authorities.
Chance of Thunderstorms with Rain in Vidarbha
Some districts in Vidarbha are expected to experience thunderstorms along with heavy rain. The weather department has issued a yellow alert for certain districts, and heavy rainfall is anticipated in various places across all districts of Vidarbha on Saturday.
Light Showers Expected in Marathwada and Central Maharashtra
On Sunday, there is a likelihood of heavy rain in some areas of Buldhana, Akola, Amravati, Nagpur, and Bhandara districts. Meanwhile, light to moderate showers are expected in most parts of Marathwada, Central Maharashtra, and Konkan, according to the weather department's forecast.
Cloudy Weather Predicted on Monday

Increased Rainfall Expected in Konkan Over the Next Two Weeks
According to the weather department's forecast for the next two weeks, there is a likelihood of above-average rainfall in Konkan. The monsoon is expected to remain active along the Konkan coast from August 13 to 20, and rainfall levels are likely to remain high from August 20 to 27 as well.
Heavy Showers Likely in Mumbai and Suburbs
The active monsoon in Konkan is also expected to impact Mumbai and its suburbs. Therefore, heavy rainfall is likely to be witnessed in Mumbai over the next few days. Residents of Mumbai have been advised to be prepared for the rain.
